QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_49

question.text: A clearing member observes that their collateral utilization is at 85%. They have pending orders worth approximately 10% of their available margin. What should they do?

answer.text: Immediately bring in additional capital / collateral to reduce utilisation before the pending orders push it past 90%
Wait until utilization reaches 90% since the exchange only acts at that level
Cancel all pending orders to reduce utilization
Switch to a different clearing corporation with lower margin requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, when collateral utilisation breaches 90% the member is moved to risk-reduction mode: all unexecuted orders are cancelled and only Immediate-or-Cancel (IOC) orders or orders that bring sufficient margin are allowed. Normal mode resumes when utilisation drops below the specified level (currently 85%). At 85% with pending orders that could add 10%, the member should respond to the exchange's alert by bringing in additional capital / collateral. The Trap: Waiting until 90% means losing all pending orders to the cancellation rule. Cancelling all orders pre-emptively disrupts strategy. Switching clearing corporations is not a real-time fix. Note: Pages 252 and 261 describe the 90% risk-reduction trigger, the cancellation of unexecuted orders, the IOC-only restriction and the alert / additional-capital response. Page 261 also notes the resumption to normal mode below the specified level.
